It is a rare genetic disorder caused by a deficiency of the enzyme alpha-N-acid galactosidase A. This enzyme is necessary for the breakdown of certain lipids in the body.

Farber disease is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern, which means that a person must inherit two copies of the mutated gene (one from each parent) to develop the condition. Carriers of the mutated gene, who have one normal and one mutated copy, are usually asymptomatic but can pass the mutated gene to their offspring.

The disease is caused by mutations in the GLA gene, which provides instructions for making the alpha-N-acid galactosidase A enzyme. When this enzyme is deficient, lipids accumulate in the body, leading to a range of symptoms, including joint pain, stiffness, and intellectual disability.
